author: ROME|King Bryan-Titan Analytics [STAR]
content:
Okay.  Here we go
...  @[AEP] Bodhitree  I don't think you are going to be able to multi account this like you think. Just from what the bare minimum they have told us... (And they obviously won't tell us everything or that would help people defeat the anti bot software.)
It sounds they are limiting cooldown to IPs.  This is extremely difficult to bypass using macro/auto clickers.  VPN are PC based so you would need to either reset your VPN every scan or use ssh tunnelling with different browsers. We are talking like maybe 2-3 accounts max.,
Programmatically would of course be easier since you could change IP on the fly but this requires extensive networking knowledge.,
2a.  If scanning does not require a signature then it may not be on chain which means you may not be able to submit a scan programmatically on chain. 

2b. If it's web2 based scanning then it's a whole nother level of complexity. You could potentially spin up browsers using web2 methods but this adds a whole other level.

Movement test is likely not running long enough to make this worthwhile. If I had time to build I'd rather focus on something guaranteed (and probably easier) like p2p trading.,
Anyone at this skill level is probably making a shit load of money running an arb bot or other systems and likely won't have time/space for this.,
I've got faith in the team. I don't think they would overlook the most simplest of bot programs.,

author: Xap✨ [STAR]
content:
One thing that people do not realize is that the most valuable creation in Tech is an "Operating System". This is what SA is. It is an operating system. People will build their "Applications" on top of it. Yes there will be Applications from SA team also. But the huge value will be created by the people innovating their own applications. 

The problem with Operating Systems are that they are very difficult to make and take a long time with multiple iterations to get it right. The supporters / Investors expect 100% all the time but the actually development is less than 20% of what the known expectations. The dev are always racing to catch up with the expectations.

This does not mean that a good visionary OS will go out of business. There will always be investment available for an OS like SA. I do not foresee any runway issue with SA. Yes due to external issues the finances can be impacted in the short term as we experienced last year. However there are very smart people sitting there to invest if SA wants. 

It all depends upon what SA team wants to give up. I do not expect them to give up too much, if any, for now. With time all of these concerns will go away and new issues will surface for us to discuss.

and yes, even if there is a single person in the room your chance can change. author: [AEP] Mendizo
content:
Personally, the risk of botting right now seems to be reduced given that there's not a sure-fire way to profit.

For example, it looks like I've spent ~0.08 SOL on transaction fees. The loot I've gotten so far is about 70 ATLAS, or 0.0085 SOL. That is a way negative ROI. This is what botters want to look for; can they consistently come out ahead? Sure, there's the very rare chance they might get loot that is worth way more (a ship), but it's not going to attract a lot of botters when there is not a guarantee. It takes time and energy to get everything setup.

Furthermore, this movement test is so different from SAGE, none of their work really carries over. That reduces the incentive even more to go full-scale botting right now, in return for what will be relative beans compared to other earning potential in SAGE.

Net/net, like Funcracker, I am happy to see what comes out of this movement test. Even if a botter wins the tankship, that's invaluable info for the team in learning what we might potentially be seeing, learning the clicks/patterns of botters, etc...
